title: Where Sky and Earth Forgot to Be Different

features.name: inversion point
features.desc-on-touch: Here the down and up have stopped meaning different things. When you look, you cannot tell if you are inside or outside the growing. The motes drift as if gravity has not decided yet which way to pull.

features.name: the suspended tower
features.desc-on-touch: A structure built into the growing, or the growing has learned to build itself into layers. Its walls rise through the same light as the air around them, and each level exists in a different understanding of which way is up.

features.name: root-sky tangle
features.desc-on-touch: The roots here grow upward and the sky hangs down in filaments. You cannot touch one without touching the other. The two have forgotten which one is holding the other up.

features.name: the breathing boundary
features.desc-on-touch: Where the two meet there is no seam. The air and the soil breathe together at the same rate. If you hold still long enough, you stop knowing which one you are breathing through.

features.name: light that grew
features.desc-on-touch: The light here came up from the ground as much as down from the sky. It is thick, almost touchable. It carries the smell of turned earth and open cloud at the same moment.

inscription: in the place where the borders learned to hold still, the border itself became the growing

reverie.title: REVERIE — the place where down became less certain
narr: You stand where the trees are so tall and so close
that up and down start to seem like a choice. She says
the roots and the clouds have made a contract — one
grows down, one grows up, but they grew so fast they
forgot which was which. And you look at her there,
reaching toward light that might be in the earth.
